scope: Final native application observed and operated through CUA; separate interactive run, not included in the three-run benchmark. The screenshot review used Fast Raster for responsive inspection.
checks: Willis Tower opens by default; loading heading reads Loading the Windy City; active geometry and navigation steps, percentage, elapsed time and random sourced fact appear.
Loading panel and facts disappear after the city appears; selected Path Tracing takes over from the initial raster preview.
Stopwatch popover lists all preparation steps and durations, actual first-city elapsed time, separate ray-resource readiness, overlapping-work explanation and detailed-report button.
City across the water selects Sunset and building lights off.
Enabling sunset lights, switching to Paris and returning to Skyline restores Sunset and lights off.
Enabling sunset lights and selecting Daylight, then reselecting City across the water restores Sunset and lights off.
Lights on the lake selects Night; the sunset-only switch is disabled, leaving the normal night lighting active.
The river leads downtown selects Golden and opens around 20 metres above the North Branch; screenshot shows river foreground between close towers.
Paris uses Loading the City of Light with no Chicago fact card.
limits: The fleeting 100% state is verified by the loading model tests and SwiftUI completion preview; it was not separately captured in this native run.
Three-second randomized rotation is checked by scheduler tests; individual facts were observed during native loading.
Earlier draft native lighting review and uncached panel inspection are not used for final performance claims.
